23:00 Local Time, 10:00 GMT, 15:30 IST: Here's the update. Match called off! India win by 4 runs (DLS method). An anticlimactic end to what promised to be a thrilling finish. "It's like batting on a trampoline at times. We weren't quite sure what height the ball was going to come through at," was how Daryl Mitchell summed up the pitch during the innings break. He was the only batter to score a half-century and he too was dropped on 21. That tells you how tough it was for the batters. After a delayed start due to rain, India opted to bowl again and bundled out the opponents for 134. Auqib Nabi accounted for the openers and Anshul Kamboj removed Nicholls to reduce NZ to 23/3. Gurnoor bowled a fiery spell - he bounced out Latham and Phillips in the same over, dismissed Santner and then added one more to finish with career-best figures of 4/30. Unlike the previous game, the tail offered no fight.

135 seemed like an easy run-chase but that wasn't the case. Duffy removed the two batters who had looked most comfortable in the previous match. Gill fell for a golden duck, while Kohli managed just 7 after opening his account with a majestic cover drive. Rohit was beaten on multiple occasions. Although he struck four boundaries, he eventually fell to Jamieson. Axar, batting at No. 5 once again, offered catching practice to third man as India slipped to 47/4. Shreyas Iyer and KL Rahul steadied the innings somewhat with a 39-run stand for the fifth wicket before the former was undone by a sharp, in-seaming bouncer from Jamieson. Naman Dhir struck a couple of fours and holed out playing the pull shot. Jamieson picked his 3rd wicket in his final over by dismissing Anshul Kamboj. With 22 runs needed 21 overs and just three wickets in hand, a new twist came in the form of rain and it failed to relent.

Gurnoor Brar | Player of the Match - (If he liked bowling here in New Zealand) I really enjoyed it. Bowling here in New Zealand, the bounce and the pace really helped me, so I enjoyed it. (On the bowling plans) obviously, in India the pitches are quite flat, so we have to bowl that hard length. But here, there's that extra bounce. So I was just bowling to my strengths, and it worked. (On the bowling plan) if you're a fast bowler bowling at an average of 140 or 142, you have to be aggressive as well. But you have to know your limits too. I just enjoy it and keep bowling. (On using the bouncer) I just try to bowl that hard length, the lengths where batters try to pull. I don't want to bowl it very high; I just keep bowling at shoulder level.

Wellington produced a batting beauty in the T20I contest between the two teams a few days ago, but with rain and moisture around, the bowlers had a field day today. The hosts were skittled out for a mere 134 while the Indians had to sweat to chase the mediocre target. Weather though had the final say and India eked out a 2-0 lead in this 5-match ODI series. We'll now move on to Hamilton for the third ODI on the 10th, with the radar promising more rain. But we'll stay hopeful as we draw curtains on this match. For now, cheers and bye..

Shubman Gill: As long as we get the win ... It wasn't easy out there. I think we bowled very well. Getting them around 130–140 was good. At one point, we thought it might be an easy target, but we kept losing wickets. We got over the line in the end.
